messages:
sam: Heads-up: rolling a config-only change to reduce per-tenant burst from 50 -> 30 and lengthen idle-request timeout from 8s -> 12s for rewrite-models in eu-central. No model binary changes. Deploy-bot scheduled for 2024-03-18T15:30:10Z. Canary: 1% -> 10% over 12m, then 30% after stabilization. Hold 20m post-ramp.

anita: Ack. Oncall (Zoe + Reece) will watch p50/p95, 5xx, downstream queue_depth. Added a temporary alert on tenant_burst_rejects.

zoe: Quick note: this config may surface client-side retries as longer timeouts. Watch client-retry-rate and overall RPS. I'll mute noisy low-volume tenants in alerting for the next hour.

sam: Canary policy (for transparency):
```
canary: {start_pct: 1, target_pct: 10, step_min: 6, final_ramp_to_30_pct_min: 12}
criteria: {p95_ms: 1500, error_rate_pct: 0.4, tenant_burst_rejects_pct: 0.1}
fallback: pin_to: rewrite-model-v0
```
(putting these in the release note)

deploy-bot: Starting canary job deploy-1710101010. Phase=canary start=1% duration=12m. Dash: https://console.redwood/deploys/1710101010

reece: Canary 7m in: p95=340ms, error_rate=0.02%, tenant_burst_rejects=0.01%. No 5xx. Increasing to 5% per plan.

zoe: Observability: queue_depth steady, no downstream backpressure. Client-retry spikes at one tenant (tenant-873) — paging dev owning that tenant to verify expected behavior.

anita: Note for rollback automation: if tenant_burst_rejects_pct > 0.2% sustained 2m OR error_rate > 0.5% for 3m, automated pin back to rewrite-model-v0 and alert oncall. Runbook: /runbooks/config-rollbacks/rewrite-burst-fallback.md

sam: Releasing release-note snippet: "Config-only: reduce tenant burst cap and extend idle timeout in eu-central for rewrite models. Added automated fallback pins and alerts. No model code change." Will tag in release notes and email channel ops.

deploy-bot: Canary complete: moving to staged ramp -> 30% over 12m. Applying config across regions after 20m hold if stable.

reece: After ramp check (now): p95=370ms, error_rate=0.03%, tenant_burst_rejects=0.02%. Looks healthy. Leaving thread open for post-deploy observations. :white_check_mark:
